title: Debugging in the browser: breakpoints, the profiler and the network tab

videos.script:
Every program you write will be wrong at some point. {{wrong}} The question is how long it takes you to find out where. Adding console.log lines and running again works, and you will keep doing it. But it is slow, and each guess costs a run.

{{tools}} The browser ships with better tools, in the developer tools window. {{pause}} A breakpoint stops the page on a line you choose and shows you every variable at that moment, and the chain of calls that led there. {{step}} From there you move one line at a time, into a function or out of it.

{{network}} The network panel shows every request the page made: what it asked for, what came back, and how long each one waited. {{profile}} The profiler shows where the time went when a page is slow, function by function.

{{lab}} In this lesson the lab asks Chromium for all of this through the same protocol the developer tools use, so you will see real pauses, real requests and real profiles in the terminal. {{method}} And it ends with a method, so that the next bug is a search rather than a guess.
